scope: Complete slow unloaded spindle demonstration of CA108r. A compliant bow and a vertically guided foot bar substitute a dimensioned modern spring-and-pull arrangement for unspecified historical dimensions. Manual feed remains locked.

date.note: Approximate manuscript dating, not a dated completion record.

folio.verification_note: Edition foliation and text verified through e-Leo. Original-holder service may be unavailable. e-Leo viewer is an authorised-edition resource, not the original holding institution.

scale_m.note: Full swept bound. All chosen dimensions are modern explanatory assumptions, never claimed measurements of a historical machine. Measured on the rebuilt lathe: the stretcher's wedges reach 0.7 m from the middle, the bed rails 0.76 m; the pole's post stands 1.66 m high; the frame runs from -0.34 m to 0.17 m deep, the ground at -0.05 m.

frame.transforms: All part positions relative to their named parent. Joint q is an extra rotation or translation about the declared parent-frame pivot applied to the rest transform. Children inherit it once.

assumptions.statement: Every numerical part size, position, orientation and support arrangement in parts is a declared modern modelling choice unless a separate primary source is explicitly attached. Materials marked assumed are plausible period choices. They are not measured from any museum replica.
assumptions.reason: Leonardo did not provide a manufacturing drawing with all dimensions.

assumptions.statement: The stated rates and loads are slow modern demonstration choices. They do not reproduce a measured speed in Leonardo s workshop.
assumptions.reason: No historical operating record was located.

assumptions.statement: The rope centreline radius is 0.04 m and its tube radius is 0.002 m, tangent to a spool of radius 0.038 m. The helical rope has 0.005 m pitch. Small axial slip is admitted in this idealised path and the shaft payout relation uses its effective radius. The spool's cheeks, the iron bushes, the bed of two rails with the poppets wedged in its slot, the slotted guides of the foot bar, the trestles and the pole's post are explicitly modern demonstration details, as are the nut's bore and the locked feed clearance.
assumptions.reason: Complete the numerical modern demonstration without presenting invented details as Leonardo dimensions.

A spring pole of ash, its butt wedged in the post's mortise, bent a little by the rope at rest. At time t each node moves in y by u(t) times s^2(3-s)/2, s its distance along the pole from the butt over the pole's length: the shape of a pole clamped at its butt and pulled at its tip, whose tip moves by u. Compliant beam approximation, not rigid hinged motion.

Top endpoint y=1.6+u and bottom endpoint y=0.20+u. Both are tangent to a single helical wrap of0.005m pitch and0.04m radius. Free straight lengths sum1.4m. Effective payout radius r_eff=0.04000791493439473m, total length1.6513771432866795m. q_spin=u/r_eff. Regenerate moving endpoints and retain wrap coordinates. This is a compliant rope approximation with small axial slip admitted along the helical wrap.

joints.notes: Length1.6513771432866795m. q_spin=u/0.04000791493439473. Endpoints bow tip and footbar. Refer to drive-rope.

input_rate.note: One deliberate foot stroke and spring return every4s. u=-0.05*(1-cos(pi*t/2))m, with period4s. Assumed spring stiffness1000N/m.

drive.justification: One deliberate foot stroke and spring return every4s. u=-0.05*(1-cos(pi*t/2))m, with period4s. Assumed spring stiffness1000N/m.

motion.visitor_12s: Three complete press-and-return cycles. Each power stroke turns the spindle0.398revolution, then reverses. No cutting or feed is simulated.

animation_notes: No bounce, no hidden energy recharge and no invisible reset.
All independent joints are in the schedule. Rigid descendants follow their parent.
Use the specified SI time without cinematic speed-up.

The rope centreline is a fixed helical wrap plus two changing free strands, with the endpoint deformation rules in drive-rope. Admit the small axial slip of this idealised helical path. Do not present it as a structural spring or rope-friction simulation. The feed screw is locked and stops 0.005 m before the spindle end.

research.identification: CA108r, perforatrice in e-Leo and drilling lathe in Vinci catalogue [EL-LATHE,LATHE-M].
research.sheet_vs_reconstruction: Sheet and later IBM Italia1952 model support a bow-return rope drive and screw advance [LATHE-M]. The guided footbar, constant-radius spool, spring stiffness and all sizes here are explicit modern simplifications. The trestles, the bed of two rails, the wedged poppets, the iron bushes, the whorl's cheeks, the slotted guides, the tall post for the pole and the drill's socket and spade are built as a workshop of the period built a pole lathe, and are ours.
research.dimensions: No Leonardo dimension or Richter number verified for the drilling machine. Nearby written labels concern the planing device, so none are borrowed [EL-LATHE].

claims.claimed_by_leonardo: Purpose inferred as drilling from machine interpretation [EL-LATHE,LATHE-M].
claims.tested_by_leonardo: No dated experiment by Leonardo was verified in the sources listed here. This is an evidence gap, not proof that he never tried it.
claims.built_in_lifetime: No lifetime build verified. IBM Italia1952 is later [LATHE-M].
claims.later_tests: No instrumented drilling test located. This is an unloaded kinematic demonstration.

inputs: Rope centreline radius r=0.04 m, stroke x=0.10 m and assumed spring stiffness k=1000 N/m [C,A-DETAIL]
physics.limits: Spring beam is schematic, not a structural model. No drilling feed, thrust, efficiency or cutting result inferred. The 5 mm helix pitch admits small axial slip. Effective payout radius is a modern kinematic approximation.
physics.verdict_en: The rope drive reverses, so continuous one-way drilling must not be shown.
physics.verdict_de: Der Seilantrieb kehrt um. Durchgehend gleichsinniges Bohren darf hier nicht gezeigt werden.
